subject: Chemistry
title: Practical Chemistry
summary: Detection of extra elements (N, S, halogens) in organic compounds uses Lassaigne's sodium fusion extract; functional groups are identified by simple colour or precipitate tests.
Inorganic salt analysis finds one cation and one anion: dilute and concentrated H₂SO₄ tests for anions, then group reagents separate cations into groups 0 to VI.
Redox titrations of KMnO₄ against oxalic acid and Mohr's salt need no indicator — KMnO₄ is its own indicator (colourless to permanent light pink).
Lab preparations (Mohr's salt, potash alum, acetanilide, p-nitroacetanilide, aniline yellow, iodoform) and the chemistry behind each step are common NEET questions.

formulas.name: KMnO₄ vs oxalic acid
formulas.note: Warm the oxalic acid to 60–70 °C; the reaction is slow at room temperature (Mn²⁺ formed then catalyses it — autocatalysis).

formulas.name: KMnO₄ vs Mohr's salt
formulas.note: Done cold — heating would oxidise Fe²⁺ by air.

formulas.name: Molarity equation for titration
formulas.formula: M₁V₁/n₁ = M₂V₂/n₂ (n = stoichiometric coefficient)  or  N₁V₁ = N₂V₂

formulas.name: Equivalent weight in acid medium
formulas.formula: KMnO₄: n-factor 5 (Mn⁺⁷ → Mn²⁺);  oxalic acid: 2;  Mohr's salt (Fe²⁺): 1

formulas.name: Dilute H₂SO₄ group (anions)
formulas.formula: CO₃²⁻ → CO₂ (lime water milky);  S²⁻ → H₂S (lead acetate paper black);  SO₃²⁻ → SO₂ (acidified K₂Cr₂O₇ green);  NO₂⁻ → brown NO₂

formulas.name: Conc. H₂SO₄ group (anions)
formulas.formula: Cl⁻ → HCl (white fumes with NH₃);  Br⁻ → reddish-brown Br₂;  I⁻ → violet I₂;  NO₃⁻ → brown ring test;  CH₃COO⁻ → vinegar smell
formulas.note: Brown ring is [Fe(H₂O)₅NO]²⁺ at the junction of conc. H₂SO₄.

formulas.name: SO₄²⁻ and PO₄³⁻
formulas.formula: SO₄²⁻ + BaCl₂ → white BaSO₄ (insoluble in HCl);  PO₄³⁻ + ammonium molybdate (HNO₃) → canary-yellow precipitate

formulas.name: Cation groups
formulas.formula: 0: NH₄⁺ (NaOH, heat → NH₃);  I: Pb²⁺ (dil. HCl);  II: Pb²⁺, Cu²⁺, As³⁺ (H₂S in acid);  III: Fe³⁺, Al³⁺ (NH₄OH + NH₄Cl);  IV: Co²⁺, Ni²⁺, Mn²⁺, Zn²⁺ (H₂S in basic);  V: Ba²⁺, Sr²⁺, Ca²⁺ ((NH₄)₂CO₃);  VI: Mg²⁺
formulas.note: Group II uses H₂S in acid (low S²⁻); group IV uses H₂S in ammoniacal medium (high S²⁻) — common ion effect.

formulas.name: Flame colours
formulas.formula: Ca brick-red;  Sr crimson;  Ba apple-green;  Cu blue-green;  Na golden-yellow;  K lilac

formulas.name: Functional group tests
formulas.formula: unsaturation: Br₂ water / Baeyer's reagent decolourised;  alcohol: ceric ammonium nitrate (red);  phenol: neutral FeCl₃ (violet);  aldehyde: Tollens', Fehling's;  carbonyl: 2,4-DNP (orange ppt);  carboxyl –COOH: NaHCO₃ (CO₂);  1° amine: carbylamine

formulas.name: Ni²⁺ and Fe³⁺ confirmations
formulas.formula: Ni²⁺ + dimethylglyoxime (NH₄OH) → red precipitate;  Fe³⁺ + K₄[Fe(CN)₆] → Prussian blue;  Fe³⁺ + KSCN → blood red

examples.title: Oxalic acid titration
examples.problem: 25 mL of 0.05 M oxalic acid is titrated with 0.02 M KMnO₄ in acid. Volume of KMnO₄?
examples.solution: Moles of oxalic acid = 0.025 × 0.05 = 1.25 × 10⁻³. MnO₄⁻ needed = (2/5) × 1.25 × 10⁻³ = 5 × 10⁻⁴ mol. Volume = 5 × 10⁻⁴/0.02 L = 25 mL.

examples.title: Mohr's salt titration
examples.problem: 20 mL of 0.1 M Mohr's salt solution is titrated with 0.02 M KMnO₄. Volume of KMnO₄?

examples.title: Why dilute H₂SO₄?
examples.problem: Why is the KMnO₄ titration done in dilute H₂SO₄ and not HCl or HNO₃?
examples.solution: HCl is oxidised by KMnO₄ to Cl₂, using up extra KMnO₄. HNO₃ is itself an oxidising agent. Dilute H₂SO₄ is neither oxidised nor oxidising.

examples.title: Group reagent logic
examples.problem: Why is NH₄Cl added before NH₄OH in group III?
examples.solution: The common ion NH₄⁺ suppresses ionisation of NH₄OH, keeping OH⁻ low enough that only the group III hydroxides (Fe³⁺, Al³⁺) precipitate, not those of groups IV–VI (e.g. Mg(OH)₂).

examples.title: Brown ring test
examples.problem: What forms the brown ring and where?
examples.solution: Nitrate solution + freshly made FeSO₄, then conc. H₂SO₄ poured down the side. A brown ring of [Fe(H₂O)₅NO]²⁺ forms where the two layers meet.

examples.title: Preparation of Mohr's salt
examples.problem: Why is a little dilute H₂SO₄ added while preparing Mohr's salt?
examples.solution: To prevent hydrolysis of FeSO₄ (and of the Fe²⁺ ion), which would make the solution turbid. Fe²⁺ is also kept from oxidising by not heating for long.

topics.title: Detection of extra elements
topics.explain: Sodium fusion converts covalent N, S and X to ionic NaCN, Na₂S and NaX. N: Prussian blue; S: violet with sodium nitroprusside or black PbS; N and S together: blood red with FeCl₃; halogens: AgNO₃ (after boiling off CN⁻ and S²⁻ with HNO₃).

topics.title: Preparation of inorganic compounds
topics.explain: Mohr's salt FeSO₄·(NH₄)₂SO₄·6H₂O and potash alum K₂SO₄·Al₂(SO₄)₃·24H₂O are double salts made by crystallising equimolar solutions; they give the tests of all their ions in water.

topics.title: Preparation of organic compounds
topics.explain: Acetanilide (aniline + acetic anhydride), p-nitroacetanilide (nitration of acetanilide at low temperature), aniline yellow (p-aminoazobenzene, coupling of benzenediazonium chloride with aniline), iodoform (ethanol or acetone + I₂ + alkali, yellow crystals).

topics.title: Chemistry of titrimetric exercises
topics.explain: Burette readings at the lower meniscus (upper for coloured KMnO₄). KMnO₄ is not a primary standard; it is standardised against oxalic acid. The end point is the first permanent pale pink colour.

topics.title: Tests for proteins and carbohydrates
topics.explain: Biuret test (violet) for proteins; Molisch's test (violet ring) for all carbohydrates; iodine test (blue) for starch; Fehling's and Benedict's for reducing sugars.

topics.title: Physical chemistry experiments (JEE)
topics.explain: Enthalpy of solution of CuSO₄ and enthalpy of neutralisation of a strong acid with a strong base (≈ −57 kJ/mol) are measured in a calorimeter from q = mcΔT. Lyophilic sols (starch, egg albumin, gum) form simply by warming with water; lyophobic sols (Fe(OH)₃, As₂S₃) need special methods such as hydrolysis or double decomposition. The rate of reaction of iodide ions with H₂O₂ is followed at room temperature (the iodine liberated turns starch blue).

topics.title: Tests for fats and oils
topics.explain: Fats leave a translucent spot on paper; the acrolein test (pungent smell on heating with KHSO₄) shows glycerol.

ratta: KMnO₄: self-indicator, colourless → pink; dil. H₂SO₄ only.
Oxalic acid titration: warm 60–70 °C; Mohr's salt: cold.
Group II: H₂S acidic;  group IV: H₂S basic.
Ni²⁺ + DMG → red;  Fe³⁺ + KSCN → blood red.
Brown ring = NO₃⁻;  canary yellow = PO₄³⁻.
Ca brick-red, Sr crimson, Ba apple-green.
